review.summary: I found no remaining defects in the two items under review. (A) The suspected MAJOR is resolved. The supplied src/app/form/[slug]/page.tsx calls verifiedRegistrationSubmission(form.id, `/form/${slug}`, query.submitted) on its own, separately from registrationRetryBoundary. When that verification succeeds, the page shows submittedVerificationMessage(form.successMessage) instead of LeadForm. The only exception is when form.fields is missing: then it shows the "paused" alert, which is intended. So the submitted state on /form never depended on retry.submitted, and the earlier finding came from reading only part of the file. (B) The fallback for older browsers is resolved. registrationAttributionFromSearchParams uses getAll and passes a plain string only when a key appears exactly once. Otherwise it passes an array: an empty one when the key is missing, or one with 2+ values when it is repeated. registrationAttribution runs each value through the per-field zod schema (z.string().…optional()), so any array fails and that field is left out. This matches how Next.js server searchParams arrays are handled, and the native and JS paths use the same rules. Empty values like `ref=` fail min(1) or the regex on both paths. In LeadForm, an attribution passed from the server boundary is used first, and the URL is read only inside the submit event, so the first server-rendered screen stays the same as the client's. Whether a source is actually eligible still depends on the unchanged submission API, and there is no LINE or other feature expansion. One optional cleanup with no effect on behaviour: the last test, "legacy browser query rejects repeated values like server searchParams", sits outside the describe block. No findings does not mean tests or release are passing: the unit, static and DB checks and the browser tests are still running and have not been verified.
